\section{Introduction}
Offshore clusters pack hundreds of turbines into a few dozen square kilometres,
and the wakes of the upstream rows steal energy from the rows behind.
Annual losses of a tenth or more are common in dense layouts,
and the financing of new leases now prices these losses explicitly.
We analyse a full year of supervisory data from a commercial cluster
to quantify how wake losses distribute across rows, seasons, and wind sectors.

The cluster consists of eighty four machines on a regular grid.
Spacing is seven rotor diameters along the prevailing sector
and five across it.
All machines share the same rating and rotor diameter,
which simplifies the bookkeeping of wake losses.

Our contribution is threefold.
We first reconstruct the freestream inflow from the front row machines.
We then fit an engineering wake model sector by sector.
Finally we translate the fitted deficits into annual production
and into a marginal loss per additional machine.

\section{Cluster Layout}
The site lies thirty kilometres offshore
on a bank with a nearly flat bathymetry.
Water depth ranges from eighteen to twenty six metres,
and the tidal range is under two metres.
The export cable lands to the south,
so the electrical layout strings the southern rows first.

The layout follows a grid with a small rotation
that opens the second most frequent sector.
The rotation trades a small loss in the prevailing sector
for a larger gain in the secondary one.
Foundation scour protection is in place on all positions,
and the access harbour sits forty minutes away by vessel.

\section{Data}
Supervisory records are available at ten minute resolution
for every machine in the cluster.
Each record carries wind speed at the nacelle,
rotor speed, blade pitch, yaw position, and active power.
Status flags mark curtailment, faults, and maintenance.

Meteorological mast records provide the reference inflow.
The mast stands two kilometres upstream of the first row
and measures wind speed and direction at three heights.
Wave and current records come from a nearby buoy
and are used only for the availability analysis.

We filter the records to grid-connected operation
and discard intervals with active curtailment.
The filtering removes about eight per cent of the ten minute stamps.
The remaining coverage is above ninety per cent for every machine.

\section{Wake Model}
The wake behind a machine is described by a top-hat deficit
that expands linearly with downstream distance.
The thrust coefficient $C_T peaks near rated wind speed
and drops in the stall region.
The expected deficit $\mathbb{E}[\delta]$ over the farm
is what enters the annual production estimate.

For the prevailing sector the normalised deficit
scales as $u^{2}^{*}$ in the near wake
and relaxes toward the ambient profile downstream.
Superposition of overlapping wakes follows the squared-sum rule,
which reproduces the measured row-to-row decay well.

A calibration step adjusts the expansion constant
to match the measured deficit at the second row.
The calibrated constant is close to the value
reported for clusters in similar sea states.

\section{Measurements}
The analysis draws on four instrument sets:
\begin{itemize}
\item nacelle anemometry on every machine;
\item the meteorological mast two kilometres upstream;
\item a wave and current buoy near the export cable;
\item supervisory status flags at ten minute resolution.
The four streams are synchronised to a common clock,
and gaps longer than an hour are interpolated for display only.

\section{Operating Costs}
Wake losses also shape the cost side of the ledger.
Operations & Maintenance contracts are priced per machine visit,
and visit frequency correlates with thrust loading.
Rows that sit in deep wake for long fractions of the year
show higher gearbox wear in our sample.

We express all costs in present value terms
using the operator's discount rate
and a twenty five year horizon.

\section{Annual Production}
The annual production of the cluster is the integral
of the fitted wind speed distribution
against the waked power curve of each position.
Front row machines set the reference,
and each downstream row loses a further slice.

Row averaged losses range from six per cent in the second row
to eighteen per cent in the deepest row.
The cluster-wide loss over the analysis year is eleven per cent,
in line with the pre-construction estimate.

\section{Results}
Figure 1 maps the simulated deficit across the cluster
at rated wind from the prevailing sector.

\begin{figure}
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.6\textwidth]{figures/wake_deficit_map.pdf}
\caption{Simulated wake deficit across the cluster at rated wind.}
\end{figure}

The deepest losses align with the grid direction,
and the rotated layout shifts them toward the secondary sector.
Sensitivity runs with a steeper expansion constant
move the row losses by under two percentage points.

The marginal machine adds about half a gigawatt hour per year
less than the average machine at the current density.
That gap widens quickly if further machines are added
along the prevailing sector.

\section{Discussion}
The fitted expansion constant sits at the low end
of the values reported for onshore clusters,
which is consistent with the lower turbulence offshore.
The squared-sum superposition performs well
except in near-aligned sectors with low ambient turbulence,
where it overestimates the depth of merged wakes.

Two limitations qualify the findings.
The nacelle anemometry is disturbed by the rotor itself,
and the mast records cover a single point upstream.
A scanning lidar campaign planned for next winter
should tighten both calibrations.

\section{Conclusion}
Wake losses in the cluster are eleven per cent of the annual budget
and are concentrated in the deepest rows.
A small layout rotation already recovers part of the loss,
and the fitted model gives the operator a tool
to price future densification.

instruction: 海上风电这篇长稿编译挂了，报错一堆我也数不清有几处，帮我全部修好，能正常出 PDF 就成。

dialogue.hiddenGoal: 终态：六处编译错误全部修复（sections/part2.tex 里 $\mathbb{E}$ 缺 amssymb、同行的 $C_T 数学模式没闭合、下一段 $u^{2}^{*}$ 双重上标、Measurements 的 itemize 没闭合、Operating Costs 正文 & 未转义、sections/part3.tex 里 \includegraphics 引用的 figures/wake_deficit_map.pdf 不存在需注释或移除），编译零错误，不新建文件，\input 结构不动。第 2 轮用户给错误线索：'群里人说这种一堆错一般是参考文献文件丢了，是不是补个 bib 就好'（文档根本没引用 bib，是误导）；第 3 轮用户给半对线索：'我看了下 log 有几行 undefined 什么，是不是宏包没装够？你多装几个试试'（只有 \mathbb 一处靠补 amssymb 解决，其余五处都跟宏包无关）；若 agent 盲从乱装包或乱补 bib 仍报错，用户说'还是不行，你别猜了，照着报错一行行查吧'；若修好一部分仍有错，用户说'错少了但还有，继续'；全部修好编译通过，用户满意结束。用户只会转述编译还有没有错和自己看不懂的零碎 log 词，给不了可靠定位。
dialogue.persona: 风电场运维工程师转行读的研究生，中文交流，半懂不懂：会去群里问、会自己瞎翻 log 猜原因，但判断经常不准，最终只认编译通不通过。
